voyager-stranis.dependency_note: She builds her own offensive buffs and Chill, but has no recovery or protection. A support that adds ATK or area vulnerability does more than merely matching her attribute.

best_partners.why: Bind increases damage taken from all-target attacks, directly helping both of Asherah’s cooldown attacks.
Cleaning Service supplies ATK Up and a Barrier that Asherah cannot provide herself.
Carmen can protect the highest-ATK carry and grant three Chill to a Moon ally with her targeted ultimate.

voyager-stranis.summary: Voyager Asherah is a straightforward area damage dealer with a single-target basic. Dawn of Night adds Chill and CRIT DMG, Veil Cleave adds SPD and gains damage at full Chill, and her upgraded passive improves critical offense as the fight develops. She is a straightforward area attacker once Chill is established.
voyager-stranis.watch: No enemy control, healing or protection.

voyager-smile.dependency_note: She supplies her own DEF Down and stack generation, but teammates that soften a durable target can make the basic-trigger condition available sooner.

best_partners.why: Star-target recovery bonuses, full targeted cleanse and team Barriers cover Smile’s lack of defenses.
Smile’s Star attacks can feed Omega’s Leap generation, while her DEF Down supports the priority target’s damage intake.
Ceres softens groups and removes a buff, making surviving low-HP targets easier for Smile to exploit.

voyager-smile.summary: Voyager Smile focuses one enemy with her basic and ultimate, then adds automatic area Cat Tapdance attacks when its HP or upgraded Leap condition is met. Those attacks and the ultimate build Smile Matrix, an ATK ramp, while the ultimate also attempts DEF Down.
voyager-smile.watch: Killing with the basic prevents its HP-condition follow-up.

voyager-oracle.dependency_note: She deals her own area damage and also improves other area attackers through Bind. Buff support enables an upgraded passive critical-damage bonus on the ultimate.

best_partners.why: Both major Asherah attacks hit all enemies and can benefit from Bind’s all-target damage vulnerability.
Light-Forged Execution benefits from landed Bind, then Amora has her own extra-turn pressure.
Cleaning Service supplies an ATK buff and Barrier to Luna, supporting the upgraded buffed-ultimate condition.

voyager-oracle.summary: Voyager Luna is an area attacker whose Bind makes enemies take more damage from all-target attacks. She builds Insight with basics and her ultimate, then uses Hecate’s Ember as a stronger full-stack payoff. Her unique potential adds a separate random-target chain-damage mechanic.
voyager-oracle.watch: Bind does not deny turns and may fail to apply.

maid-lantern.dependency_note: She starts with her own Umbral Echo window and can attack independently. Healing is still valuable after the lethal-hit response; a buff provider improves damage but is not a required trigger.

best_partners.why: Ceres can heal Carnelia after Spoke leaves her near minimum HP and adds cleanse and team ATK Up.
Emily's targeted Barrier and ATK buff protect Carnelia before or after her survival response.
Seira can grant Carnelia Greater ATK Up and progress toward her next turn, supporting a selected damage window.
Bell removes existing buffs while Carnelia blocks future buffs, covering different parts of enemy buff management.

maid-lantern.summary: Carnelia is an area-damage caster with a strong opening and a once-per-battle survival response. Umbral Echo improves her area ultimate and makes Guiding Twilight repeat once against a random enemy. Her special also blocks buffs and reduces enemy progress toward the next turn, giving her control beyond damage.
maid-lantern.watch: The extra special target is random.

maid-bell.dependency_note: Her disruption functions without a specific attribute team. ACC Down has real synergy with Fei's evasion, and Star attacks support Dana, while healers protect Bell's relatively offensive build.

best_partners.why: Kyra's Price of Silence gains damage against a Silenced target, giving Bell's Silence a direct offensive payoff.
Bell's ACC Down can help Fei evade attacks and trigger Lunar Shadow.
Bell's Star attacks feed Dana's Leap; Dana can buff Bell if Bell is the highest-ATK other ally.
Ceres heals and cleanses Bell while adding team ATK Up, preserving the control slot through incoming area damage.

maid-bell.summary: Bell is a fast control attacker whose main value is disrupting enemy buffs and cooldown skills. Condolence hits the whole team, lowers ACC when it lands and grants Bell SPD Up. Encoffin strips one target's buffs and attempts Silence, while any other unit's defeat feeds her next-turn progress and ATK.
maid-bell.watch: Area ACC Down remains probabilistic even at the highest level.

maid-twohander.dependency_note: Her targeted Barrier and ATK buff fit a damage carry, while a real healer/cleanser covers attrition and debuffs. Incoming area attacks feed her loop; allies do not need to share her attribute to use the Barrier.

best_partners.why: Ceres supplies real healing and cleansing while Emily supplies a targeted Barrier and party DEF Up.
Carnelia is a useful recipient for Cleaning Service's ATK buff and Barrier, including after her lethal-hit response.
Emily can protect the marked attacker or Lydia; her own area ultimate also feeds Lydia if Emily actually receives Passing the Buck.
Seira can accelerate another carry with Greater ATK Up while Emily protects it; avoid treating overlapping ATK buffs as automatically additive.

maid-twohander.summary: Emily is an HP-scaling defender who protects a chosen attacker while building repeated area damage. Cleaning Service supplies ATK Up and a Barrier without giving up Emily's next action, and incoming attacks reduce her ultimate cooldown. Turn-Down Service builds Awakened Memory, making later ultimates more threatening.

kingdom-knight.dependency_note: Use her beside an attacker who needs CRIT Rate and ATK, with a healer covering survival. Pairing only with fully self-buffed attackers wastes much of Vow's value.

best_partners.why: Charlotte's attacking Sun ultimate feeds Cristelle's Ignition and supplies ATK Down for the chain-damage debuff count.
Carnelia can receive Vow's CRIT Rate and ATK buffs to support an area-damage turn.
Ceres provides healing and cleanse.
Emily adds a Barrier for the carry and party DEF Up while Charlotte supplies CRIT Rate.

kingdom-knight.summary: Charlotte mixes single-target damage with a buff for one ally. Vow of Victory gives CRIT Rate Up, an upgrade-dependent ATK buff and an extra turn for Charlotte herself. Unyielding Strike weakens enemy ATK, advances Charlotte's next turn and gradually improves her basic through the higher-level passive.
kingdom-knight.watch: ATK Up on Vow is probabilistic until its later upgrades.

kingdom-shielder.dependency_note: She needs a healer because drawing attacks does not restore HP. Pairing with a damage dealer who needs DEF Up makes more sense than stacking several protectors without enough damage.

best_partners.why: Ceres supplies the healing and cleansing Carmen lacks, with party ATK Up to compensate for a defensive slot.
Frey heals and shields Carmen, and can fully cleanse the defender when control threatens her next Taunt.
Carnelia supplies area damage and Buff Block while party DEF Up reduces incoming pressure.
Bell provides buff removal and Silence, giving control options beyond a single Taunt.

kingdom-shielder.summary: Carmen in her ordinary knight variant is an HP-scaling defender who tries to force one enemy into a basic attack through Taunt. Her ultimate also gives everyone DEF Up, while Shock Therapy reinforces her own DEF and Effect Hit. Chill makes her tougher at higher passive levels.
kingdom-shielder.watch: No ordinary healing or Barrier in this variant.

kingdom-pray.dependency_note: Star allies get extra healing, but she can heal any attribute. Choose her for Barrier coverage and one-target cleansing rather than filling a team with Star units that have no other synergy.

best_partners.why: Haydee shares damage and needs healing; Frey's enhanced Star-ally recovery and full cleanse help keep the protector functioning.
Dana is a Star attacker who receives stronger healing and adds ally ATK support that Frey lacks.
Bell benefits from enhanced Star healing, while providing Silence and buff removal in return.
Emily supplies offensive support and area damage; Frey supplies the healing and cleansing Emily does not actually list.

kingdom-pray.summary: Frey is an HP-scaling healer with two different jobs: Rapid Resupply fully cleanses one ally, while Monastir's All-Out Support heals and shields the group. Star allies receive more healing. At higher passive levels maximum Leap also turns her basic into an automatic small party recovery and self turn-progress tool.
kingdom-pray.watch: No direct party cleanse in the ultimate.

nightmare-reaper.dependency_note: Choose a carry whose next attack benefits from a stronger ATK buff and turn progress. Seira supplies no listed healing or Barrier, so a sustain/protection partner remains important.

best_partners.why: Carnelia can turn Greater ATK Up and ally turn progress into an earlier or stronger area-damage window.
Lydia benefits from offensive support, and Seira can instead buff Lydia's marked attacker to help its turns.
Emily shields the chosen carry and adds party DEF Up while Seira supplies stronger offensive support.
Ceres supplies healing and cleanse, leaving Seira free to use her non-attacking support skill.

nightmare-reaper.summary: Seira is a support attacker who gives one ally Greater ATK Up and progress toward its next turn, then gains an extra turn herself. She can follow with single-target damage and SPD Down. Her unique potential, if obtained, turns the non-attacking buff skill into additional Nova Force and personal Toughness damage.

stellar-thief.dependency_note: She can build her own stacks and buffs, but teammates that soften targets or protect her make kill-based resets more plausible.

best_partners.why: Cleaning Service adds ATK Up and a Barrier to improve Trish’s survival and finishing damage.
Area damage can soften targets while dispel and Isolation reduce enemy protection before Trish commits.
Oath protects Trish if she is highest ATK; healing and Barriers help keep the finisher alive.

stellar-thief.summary: Trish is a single-target finisher who builds Leap, advances her own turns and spends stacks on DEF penetration. Killing with Continuous Cuts resets that skill, so choosing a finishable target is more important than using the ultimate as soon as it lights up.
stellar-thief.watch: Reset depends on her actually defeating the target.

eastern-swordmaster.dependency_note: She can run a personal focused-damage branch alone, but the support branch specifically rewards other Star allies who use Leap or crit damage. Choose the branch for the fight rather than automatically stacking identical attributes.

best_partners.why: Lyn's Clear Wind special can give Tanya three Leap toward Demolition Mode; the team crit-damage buff also supports Tanya's attacks.
Star Mina can receive distributed Leap to reach her special's extra-Bleed condition and CRIT DMG support for her direct attacks.
Kingdom Frey supplies healing, a full single-target cleanse and party barriers, with increased recovery for Star allies such as Lyn.

eastern-swordmaster.summary: Lyn is a Star attacker with two purposeful branches. Phantom Blade Dance first grants Bright Moon for a stronger focused ultimate; Clear Wind Bright Moon first stays area damage and grants Star-team crit-damage support plus Clear Wind, enabling later Leap support. Skill order changes what the team gets.
eastern-swordmaster.watch: Wrong branch can trade away needed wave coverage or team buffs.

incognita-landgrave.dependency_note: Other allies must attack to trigger Seething Vengeance. Attacking Sun special/ultimate skills accelerate Ignition more than non-Sun ones; a healer's non-attacking support cast does not meet that condition.

best_partners.why: Scarlet applies Burn and her attacking Sun cooldown skills feed Cristelle's Ignition; Cristelle can extend Burn on their shared target.
Kyra's Sun cooldown attacks feed Ignition and add Silence and ATK Down for Nightmare Unleashed's debuff count.
Charlotte's Unyielding Strike is an attacking Sun ultimate and adds ATK Down; Vow of Victory is non-attacking and should not be counted as an Ignition trigger.
Ceres supplies healing, cleanse and team ATK Up, but her support skills do not count as attacking Sun cooldown skills.

incognita-landgrave.summary: Cristelle is a Sun debuff-and-chain-damage specialist. Allies' attacking cooldown skills build her Ignition, then Seething Vengeance triggers automatically at maximum stacks to spread Burn and advance her next turn. Her ultimate rewards an already debuffed target with extra chain-damage instances and longer Burn.
incognita-landgrave.watch: Reactive special cannot be manually scheduled independently of allies.

incognita-flower.dependency_note: Her self-sustain tools are Barriers, not healing. Pair her with a healer and attackers who benefit from the damage she absorbs; piling on another Guard source does not add their percentages together.

best_partners.why: Frey heals Haydee, can fully cleanse her, and grants Barriers; Haydee is also eligible for Frey's enhanced Star-ally healing.
Ceres's party healing helps cover shared damage and her cleanse supports Haydee's defensive uptime.
Haydee's ACC Down can help Fei evade attacks and trigger Lunar Shadow when the debuff sticks.
Carnelia supplies damage and Buff Block while Haydee shares incoming damage to protect her outside Spoke's survival window.

incognita-flower.summary: Haydee is a DEF-scaling protector who takes part of allies' damage through Guard, shields herself, and attacks with DEF scaling. Her useful sequence is to maintain a Barrier, then use Thorned Grave for Guard and stronger damage; she can turn maximum Leap into an extra turn with Spiked Armor.
incognita-flower.watch: No heal replenishes damage taken through Guard.

eastern-owl.dependency_note: Bring damage dealers and protection appropriate to the encounter. Sun allies receive more healing from his ultimate; a Burn user can feed his upgraded passive, and a separate cleanser is important against heavy debuffs.

best_partners.why: Serpang's Sun turns feed Charlotte's Ignition and his ultimate heals Sun allies more effectively; Charlotte supplies team ATK Up for offense.
Marcille applies Burn, which can feed Serpang's upgraded passive on enemy turns, while he heals and can lower resistance for her debuffs.
Hilde supplies opening ally barriers and self-protection; Serpang restores lost HP and can weaken a threatening enemy's ATK.

eastern-owl.summary: Serpang is an HP-scaling Sun healer who weakens one enemy and protects himself plus a low-HP teammate from skill damage. His upgraded passive links Burn on enemies to Ignition generation, then spends five Ignition to move much closer to another turn.
eastern-owl.watch: No cleanse, revive or party barrier.

apostle-gille.dependency_note: Bring an ally who supplies their own Shatter, and enough survival to exploit break windows. Dark Asherah and Tyria qualify through their ultimates; an arbitrary Chaos ally does not.

best_partners.why: Lucula Noctis supplies her own three-turn Shatter; Phantom Sever has extra boss Toughness damage while it lasts, directly supporting Gille's break-state loop.
Crescendo of Sorrow supplies Shatter, allowing Overture access; Tyria's marked-target attacks can exploit the resulting broken window.
Bal Doré heals while attacking and Lumière Sonnet cleanses and advances teammates, helping the team reach another break cycle.

apostle-gille.summary: Gille is a break-team coordinator who also deals area damage. She turns Shatter users into a small orchestra: Overture adds Toughness damage, Imperfect Deathcry upgrades that state, and Malice rewards attacks into broken targets. Pick her after choosing Shatter users, not before.
apostle-gille.watch: Allied Shatter is a real selection constraint, not a benefit given to every teammate.

magician-druid.dependency_note: She can attack alone, but attacking Star allies accelerate her specific Leap engine. Healing and protection remain external; choose Star partners for actual useful attacks and support, not only their attribute.

best_partners.why: Bell's Star attacks feed Dana's Leap while providing Silence, buff removal and area damage.
Haydee's Star attacks feed Leap and her Guard protects Dana through her slower start.
Frey supplies Barriers and enhanced healing for Star Dana; her basic attacks can feed Leap, but her non-attacking heals do not.
Carnelia offers complementary area pressure and can receive Rapid Bloom's ally ATK buff if she is the highest-ATK other ally.

magician-druid.summary: Dana is an area-damage caster who also buffs the highest-ATK other ally. Star allies' attacks build her Leap at higher passive levels, and full Leap becomes Roroca!, an ATK/CRIT DMG boost. Critical hits can grant SPD Up, so her damage, team composition and turn frequency support one another.
magician-druid.watch: Low maximum SPD makes opening order a build concern.

saintess-demon.dependency_note: Debuff partners supply both the special’s damage bonus and effects worth extending. Sun allies’ attacks feed Ignition only after the passive gains that feature.

best_partners.why: Unknown Hex and SPD Down provide several useful effects for Muriel to extend on the priority target.
Sun attacks feed upgraded Triumphant while Luna supplies DEF Down, ATK Down and defensive support.
Harley can grant three Ignition to the highest-ATK Sun ally and provides speed/turn control; ensure that recipient is Muriel.

saintess-demon.summary: Muriel combines area damage and ATK Down with a single-target debuff extender. She is most useful when teammates place several meaningful debuffs first, then she keeps one target’s debuffs alive while Sun allies help build Ignition for her Burn condition. Use Muriel after allies have already applied debuffs worth preserving.
saintess-demon.watch: Extension has little value without useful existing debuffs.

saintess-elf.dependency_note: She keeps an important ally fighting but needs damage dealers and preferably another source of party-wide recovery or cleanse.

best_partners.why: Her non-attack heal and ultimate feed Lugh’s Snow Blossom before Swift Decree.
Carmen supplies party recovery through basics and targeted cleanse, covering gaps in Elisa’s support.
Ceres disrupts enemy turns while Elisa restores or revives the damage/control carry.

saintess-elf.summary: Elisa is a targeted healer and reviver whose Holy Blessing reduces damage and raises Effect RES. Her ultimate can rescue a fallen ally or accelerate a living one, while her upgraded passive rewards staying healthy and managing Agitation for an extra turn.
saintess-elf.watch: No cleanse in her own kit.

apostle-tyria.dependency_note: She supplies her own marks, Ignition and Shatter, but needs protection and benefits from extra basic attacks rather than teammates with matching names or attributes alone.

best_partners.why: Song of the Toast gives team ATK Up; Charlotte also gains Ignition when Tyria's Sun turn starts, creating a concrete reciprocal interaction.
A highest-ATK Tyria can be pulled into a dual attack after Black or White, giving Prelude another opportunity to apply Thorns.
Party healing and a two-debuff cleanse protect the caster whose death removes Thorns.

apostle-tyria.summary: Tyria is a mark-driven attacker with both area setup and focused finishing damage. Crescendo of Sorrow seeds Thorns of Ruin, then her basic adds marks and can automatically trigger Requiem of Ruin at three stacks. Defender-class targets give her an additional damage condition.
apostle-tyria.watch: Losing Tyria also removes her Thorns from enemies.

recon-knuckle.dependency_note: Her basic and ultimate function without a special ally, but frequent enemy area attacks are what unlock the reaction’s value. Team healing remains useful.

best_partners.why: Oath can protect Roberta if she is highest ATK; reaction healing and Barriers help her survive incoming pressure.
Star-target healing bonuses and a full targeted cleanse complement Roberta’s one-debuff self-cleanse.
Roberta’s attacks on a surviving Aqua Bomb target can enable Smile’s reaction when Smile has enough Leap.

recon-knuckle.summary: Roberta is a single-target attacker who retaliates automatically against all-target attacks. Critical hits make that reaction cycle faster, while her skills push her toward her next turn and her unique potential can turn critical skill damage into self-healing.
recon-knuckle.watch: Fast Track loses relevance if enemies avoid all-target attacks.

recon-amulet.dependency_note: Non-attack allies build Snow Blossom before Swift Decree. Nova Force availability and turn order determine how much of the slash window is usable.

best_partners.why: Her two non-attack support skills can seed Snow Blossom while healing and cleansing.
Targeted heal and revive/support are non-attacks that feed flowers before Swift Decree.
Cleaning Service is a non-attack that adds a Barrier and ATK Up while helping the flower setup.

recon-amulet.summary: Lugh turns allies’ non-attack skills into Snow Blossom, then activates Swift Decree to replace her basic with Subdual Slash. Her damage window depends on managing those stacks and Nova Force, with DEF Down and ultimate delay as added utility.
recon-amulet.watch: Ten-turn ultimate cooldown makes careless usage costly.

independent-vagabond.dependency_note: She supplies her own evasion and ATK buff, but does not heal. ACC Down from Haydee or Bell is a functional partner effect; a healer is still needed when evasion fails.

best_partners.why: Haydee's ACC Down can support evasion, and Guard shares damage when Fei is hit.
Bell's area ACC Down can make multiple enemies less accurate; her Silence and buff removal can disrupt an accuracy-buffer.
Ceres heals failed dodges and cleanses debuffs that interfere with Fei's next action.
Frey offers a direct full cleanse and Barriers instead of relying on evasion to prevent every hit.

independent-vagabond.summary: Fei is an evasive single-target attacker. A successful evasion triggers Lunar Shadow against the attacker, builds Chill and grows her passive ATK. Her ultimate spends Chill for a burst with DEF penetration at full stacks; she is strongest when enemies attack her and can actually miss.
independent-vagabond.watch: Miss-dependent reactions can disappear against accuracy tools.

grace-dualsword.dependency_note: She manages her own debuffs and attack buffs. Moon allies with reliable crits help build Chill, while a defender/healer supplies the team utility and sustain her self-focused kit lacks.

best_partners.why: All In improves Moon teammates' crit consistency, helping feed Noble Bearing; Epindel's Moon attacks also feed Frey's Cash In.
Claire's own crit ramp makes her a plausible Moon critical-hit source for Chill, while the pair focus a durable target.
Moon Emily supplies targeted barrier/ATK Up and party DEF Up, filling defensive jobs Epindel's self-cleanse cannot cover.

grace-dualsword.summary: Ordinary Epindel is a Moon focused attacker who rewards attacking while free of debuffs. Relentless Effort removes two debuffs from herself, grants ATK Up/Immunity and an extra turn; Hawk of Orlan then gains damage if she is clean. Moon ally crits feed Chill for her basic payoff.
grace-dualsword.watch: No area attack, party recovery or team cleanse.

starpiercer-omega.dependency_note: Star allies directly feed Auto-Hunt System. Include attackers who take turns, not just a full roster of non-attack supports.

best_partners.why: A Star attacker whose basic and reaction pressure can supply allied attack opportunities while DEF Down helps damage.
Star single-target pressure and automatic reactions can feed Omega’s passive when the appropriate attacks occur.
Frey’s recovery is enhanced on Star allies and supplies the cleanse Omega lacks; her support turns themselves are non-attacks.

starpiercer-omega.summary: Omega builds Leap from her attacks and other Star allies’ attacks, then converts full Leap at turn start into Power-Up Star. Those stars make Mega Punch! repeat, so she is a ramping area attacker rather than an immediate opening nuke. Build a Star attacking core before treating repeated punches as dependable damage.
starpiercer-omega.watch: Ramp is gated by her turn starts, not just the number of ally attacks.

bunny-knight.dependency_note: Her core attacks work without a Sun party, but allied Sun turns directly generate Ignition. Choose Sun allies who also supply protection, healing or damage rather than four attackers merely for the attribute.

best_partners.why: Every allied Sun Tyria turn supplies Ignition; Tyria also uses Charlotte's team ATK Up for her mark-based damage.
Hilde's Sun turns feed Ignition while opening ally barriers cover Charlotte's setup turn.
Serpang's Sun turns feed Ignition, and his party heal gives enhanced recovery to Sun allies.

bunny-knight.summary: Bunny Charlotte is a Sun single-target attacker who also buffs the party's ATK. Song of the Toast grants a DEF-penetrating Lucky Token and an extra turn; while the token lasts, her own-turn basic repeats once. Sun teammates help refill Ignition for Cornered Rabbit.
bunny-knight.watch: No area attack, cleanse or ordinary healing.

west-beamsword.dependency_note: Her control works without a required attribute partner. She still needs protection and enough speed to act before a dangerous enemy; Moon allies add useful interactions rather than unlocking her basic function.

best_partners.why: Bunny Frey supplies party CRIT Rate and gains turn progress and High Roller stacks after other Moon allies attack, including Ceres.
Wedding Carmen supplies healing and cleansing that Ceres lacks, and her Wedding March gives additional Chill to Moon allies.
Bell removes all buffs from one priority enemy and applies Silence, complementing Ceres's one-buff removal across the entire group.
Summer Luna adds team defense and reactive disruption against critical attackers, buying time for Ceres's next control cycle.

west-beamsword.summary: Western Ceres is an offensive controller: she removes a buff from every enemy, slows them with Freeze, then pushes a dangerous target away from its next turn. Her biggest advantage is creating another opportunity to act before the opponent. She is not the healing Maid Ceres variant.
west-beamsword.watch: No healing, Barrier or damage sharing for teammates.

west-rod.dependency_note: A teammate who establishes a debuff before Lydia's basic makes her loop easier to start. She benefits from extra basic attacks and needs a healer or protector; a Chaos-only lineup is not required.

best_partners.why: Rosaria's group DEF Down establishes debuffs and adds burst damage while Lydia works on slowing targets. Lydia's Hex can help later debuff attempts, but cannot retroactively help a debuff already checked.

Waltz Asherah supplies healing and cleansing, and her rising Dual Attack chance can create more opportunities for allied basic attacks rather than forcing Lydia to spend every turn on a cooldown skill.
Emily's targeted Barrier and ATK buff can protect a fragile damage slot while Lydia supplies the slowing effects that Emily lacks.

west-rod.summary: Original Lydia is a durable debuffer who makes enemies act more slowly and become easier to debuff. Unknown Hex is the center of her kit: establish a debuff, then her basic can keep applying Hex while her passive builds ATK. Her maximum HP is 39,345, but that is personal bulk rather than protection for allies.
west-rod.watch: An established debuff is needed to start the basic's Hex interaction.

detective-professor.dependency_note: Choose a carry whose basic is useful and make that ally the intended highest ATK. The team also needs enough attacking actions to refill Chill and a defender/healer to survive the cycle.

best_partners.why: A forced Prelude basic can add Thorns and potentially trigger Tyria's marked-target Requiem; both have explicit basic/follow-up reasons to work together.
Gwen gains Electric Shock from allied attacks and an extra stack from special attacks while in Standby; Professor M supplies repeated attacking actions and marks special vulnerability.
Emily's targeted ATK Up/barrier can support the intended highest-ATK carry while party DEF Up helps preserve the attack engine.

detective-professor.summary: Professor M is an attack enabler who repeatedly brings the highest-ATK ally into the fight. Her basic grants that ally Sample Behavior Analysis and forces a dual attack; other allies' attacks feed her Chill and next-turn progress. At full Chill, an allied attack automatically triggers Evil Begets Evil.
detective-professor.watch: Highest-ATK targeting may select the wrong ally without tuning.

detective-sheriff.dependency_note: Use allies who attack often, especially with special skills, while keeping at least one other ally alive for Standby. A defender and healer protect against damage that targeting protection does not stop.

best_partners.why: Repeated attacking actions help build shocks; The Magic Bullet adds special-skill vulnerability for Gwen's manual and triggered special attacks.
Claire's manual and triggered Where Are You Looking? supply special-skill attacks while contributing focused damage, helping feed Gwen's Standby resource.
Bal Doré heals while attacking with a special skill, contributing shock generation while recovery and cleanse help preserve other allies.

detective-sheriff.summary: Gwen is a protected follow-up attacker who watches teammates build Electric Shock. While On-Site Standby is active, allied attacks add shocks and special attacks add an extra stack; reaching five lets her automatically use Light of Truth!. Her ultimate refreshes Standby and triggers that special immediately.
detective-sheriff.watch: Area damage still reaches her and she cannot keep Standby protection alone.

wild-hog.dependency_note: Use a Sun attacker if you want the special's three Ignition stacks to benefit a teammate. Bring recovery or stronger protection when incoming burst can kill allies before her tempo buffs matter.

best_partners.why: Bunny Charlotte benefits from Harley's Sun turns and can use three supplied Ignition stacks if she is the highest-ATK Sun ally.
Muriel gains Ignition when another Sun ally attacks and rewards an already-debuffed target, so Harley's attacks and tempo control fit her sustained Sun plan.
Maid Ceres heals Harley back toward the healthy Chicken Race branch and supplies cleansing absent from Harley's own kit.

wild-hog.summary: Harley is a tempo defender: she gives the team DEF Up, delays enemy turns and can speed allies up while healthy. Her special feeds Ignition to the highest-ATK Sun ally. She is better understood as a support for a Sun offense than as a defender who catches every attack for the team.
wild-hog.watch: No Taunt, party healing or ally Barrier to directly rescue a carry.

construct-bomb.dependency_note: Petra builds her own Ignition; a separate breaker becomes useful once her upgraded passive rewards allied breaks. She needs defensive support rather than three other attackers just to fill stacks.

best_partners.why: Charlotte gives party ATK Up and uses Petra's DEF Down; Petra's Sun turns also build Charlotte's Ignition.
Tanya can finish a break to activate Petra's upgraded passive and provides team CRIT Rate Up before damage.
Serpang heals Petra with the Sun bonus, lowers enemy ATK and Effect RES, and helps sustain a slower boss plan.

construct-bomb.summary: Petra is a straightforward Sun single-target attacker who brings DEF Down for the rest of the team. Breaking Ground accelerates her and builds Ignition; Construction Negotiations spends those stacks for extra damage while attempting a two-turn defense reduction.
construct-bomb.watch: No area damage, healing, cleanse or protection.

bunny-scissors.dependency_note: She supplies her own random balls and Ignition. External buffs improve Ready and Willing! if that potential is available, and a healer/defender covers her lack of sustain.

best_partners.why: Song of the Toast supplies party ATK Up, one useful buff for Ready and Willing!; Scarlet's Sun turns also feed Charlotte's Ignition.
Cleaning Service provides both a targeted barrier and ATK Up; Turn-Down Service adds party DEF Up, helping Scarlet survive and furnishing distinct buffs.
Serpang heals with a Sun bonus and can lower one enemy's Effect RES, supporting Scarlet's debuff attempts without promising a bypass.

bunny-scissors.summary: Bunny Scarlet disrupts healing and removes one enemy buff while contributing area damage. Her turn-start pinball rolls determine whether Anyway, I Won! gets a shorter cooldown or a full reset; she is a reactive utility attacker rather than a predictable burst rotation.
bunny-scissors.watch: Random ball results prevent a dependable ultimate-reset schedule.

bunny-spear.dependency_note: She supplies ATK Up, critical buffs and her own Chill loop. External early crit support makes the special's three-Chill condition more reliable; survival support remains necessary.

best_partners.why: All In gives early CRIT Rate Up for Claire's special; Claire's Moon attacks feed Frey's Cash In resource and next-turn progress.
The Magic Bullet adds special-skill vulnerability, useful for Where Are You Looking?; a highest-ATK Claire can also be called into basics.
Emily protects Claire with Cleaning Service and provides ATK Up, allowing Claire to prioritize crit consistency over trying to tank.

bunny-spear.summary: Bunny Claire is a focused Moon attacker whose crits generate resources and faster turns. Bunny Jackpot starts a three-turn crit buff, Where Are You Looking? adds three Chill on a crit, and a basic used at full Chill can trigger that special automatically. Use Claire (Flawless Blue Rose) against one durable opponent.
bunny-spear.watch: No area attack for broad wave clear.

summer-oracle.dependency_note: Her reactive value depends on enemy critical hits against teammates. Add real healing and carry damage; her own shields do not recover the whole party.

best_partners.why: Luna’s Sun attacks feed upgraded Triumphant, while Muriel can extend Luna’s DEF Down or ATK Down.
Party healing and two-debuff cleanse cover sustain and cleansing missing from Luna’s kit.
Harley supplies additional turn pressure and team speed; avoid overvaluing duplicate DEF Up.

summer-oracle.summary: Summer Luna protects allies from critical damage at the start of battle and reacts when another ally takes a critical hit. She combines HP-based attacks, personal Barriers, team DEF Up and single-target ATK Down/Taunt, with stronger reaction damage at full Ignition.
summer-oracle.watch: Reaction requires another ally to suffer a critical hit.

summer-smile.dependency_note: Other allies must attack the marked target while it survives. Her unique potential helps Leap supply but is an acquired effect, not part of the ordinary passive.

best_partners.why: Frequent single-target attacks and eligible reactions can pressure the Aqua Bomb target while Smile has Leap.
Dispel and turn disruption can expose the marked enemy for Smile and allies to focus.
Star-enhanced healing and cleanse help Smile remain active; support non-attacks do not trigger Heat Control.

summer-smile.summary: Summer Smile marks one enemy with Aqua Bomb and follows allies’ attacks on that survivor with Heat Control when she has enough Leap. Those reactions build Sparkler, which her ultimate spends on additional Heat Control instances. Use Smile (Sunshine Cat) in a party that can focus the marked enemy without instantly killing it.
summer-smile.watch: Trigger fails if the ally kills the marked enemy.

independent-dragon.dependency_note: Her ATK buff, SPD buff and conditional self-heal are self-contained. A healer still covers burst, and a taunting ally can reduce the number of marked attacks she personally receives.

best_partners.why: Frey adds Barriers and a full one-target cleanse, covering damage that Lacy's conditional self-heal cannot handle.
Ceres heals and cleanses while leaving Lacy free to take marked attacks.
Dana can give ATK Up to the highest-ATK other ally, supporting Lacy's damage and ATK-based self-heal if she receives it.
Bell strips buffs and Silences a dangerous enemy while Lacy focuses a marked target.

independent-dragon.summary: Lacy combines fast single-target attacks with a team-wide Entangled Dream debuff. That mark weakens enemy ATK and makes attacks into Lacy feed her healing and next-turn progress. She has substantial personal tools, but the response loop only works when marked enemies actually attack her.
independent-dragon.watch: No party heal or direct ally protection.

construct-gadget.dependency_note: She can attack alone, but her reason to occupy a team slot is break timing plus brief crit support. Let teammates lower Toughness without stealing a planned Tanya break when the upgraded passive is available.

best_partners.why: Tanya's own break triggers Petra's upgraded ally-break passive, while Petra applies DEF Down for Tanya's attacks.
Lyn's Clear Wind branch distributes three Leap to Star allies, helping Tanya reach Demolition Mode, and can buff Star allies' crit damage.
Team healing helps maintain Fried Food Party's HP condition, and Lumière Sonnet cleanses and advances Tanya's next turn.

construct-gadget.summary: Tanya is a Star focused attacker who can turn her own breaks into ally turn progress. Buzz-Buzz Chainsaw offers brief team crit support; after enough Leap, her upgraded passive enters Demolition Mode and Bang-Bang Bunker gains additional Toughness damage.
construct-gadget.watch: Main break engine is absent at passive level 1.

detective-watson.dependency_note: Use other Moon allies who can survive being attacked if you want the upgraded passive's Chill generation. She needs actual healing and personal protection because the barrier skill protects everyone except her.

best_partners.why: Emily is a Moon defender who can give Lily a targeted barrier, covering the self-exclusion of Precious Moment; attacks into Emily can feed Lily's upgraded passive.
Frey gives team crit support and benefits from Lily's Moon attacks through Cash In; Frey still does not replace a healer.
Party healing/cleanse keeps Lily alive while she prepares Consulting, and turn progress helps recover from her low stored SPD.

detective-watson.summary: Lily is a Moon area attacker with a supportive barrier skill. Lily's Precious Moment shields the other allies and gives her a personal crit/speed state; Mr. Rabbit's Instant Verdict then gains damage while that state is active and can lower enemy ATK.
detective-watson.watch: The barrier skill excludes Lily herself.

mutant-mask.dependency_note: She can establish Stealth and Silence herself, but an allied Silence provider improves timing. A healer and actual protection cover area damage; a team that simply leaves her last alive removes Stealth's targeting protection.

best_partners.why: Bell's two-turn Silence can supply a longer window for Price of Silence's damage bonus and removes enemy buffs.
Kyra's Sun attacking cooldown skills feed Cristelle's Ignition; ATK Down and Silence add debuffs for chain damage.
Ceres heals area damage and cleanses Kyra without relying on Stealth to prevent every hit.
Emily's Barrier protects Kyra against damage Stealth does not avoid and supplies an ATK buff when needed.

mutant-mask.summary: Kyra is a single-target disruptor who uses Stealth to gain damage and delay an enemy's next turn. Distorted Attention gives her Stealth and attempts Silence plus ATK Down; Price of Silence then rewards both her own Stealth and a Silenced target. Allies can also supply Silence so the payoff is not limited to her short window.
mutant-mask.watch: Silence window can expire before her next turn.

dress-stranis.dependency_note: She supports almost any team that needs recovery, cleanse and turn progress. Choose teammates whose offense benefits from staying active; do not select her as a substitute for a specialized damage dealer.

best_partners.why: Emily's barriers and DEF Up reduce incoming damage, while Asherah restores HP and removes debuffs that Emily's kit does not explicitly cleanse.
Bal Doré is an attacking special that contributes to Gwen's Electric Shock during Standby, while healing keeps Gwen's other allies alive.
Healing and cleanse keep the break carry active; Lumière Sonnet's allied turn progress helps reach Shatter/break windows without requiring shared damage roles.

dress-stranis.summary: Dress Asherah is an HP-scaling healer and cleanser, not the damage-focused Voyager or Dark variants. Bal Doré heals while attacking; Lumière Sonnet heals the party, removes two debuffs and helps other allies reach their next turns. Her upgraded passive makes basic attacks contribute targeted recovery.
dress-stranis.watch: No revive, barrier or complete prevention of incoming debuffs.

wedding-shielder.dependency_note: Build ATK ordering around the intended oath carry and keep Carmen alive through redirected damage. She protects a damage plan rather than replacing a damage dealer.

best_partners.why: A Moon carry can receive three Chill from Wedding March, directly strengthening Blade Gale’s Chill-based turn reduction.
Wedding March is a non-attack that can feed Lugh’s Snow Blossom before Swift Decree, while oath protection helps the slash setup.
Carmen can protect Amora as the highest-ATK ally and remove debuffs that would suppress Amora’s clean-state damage bonus.

wedding-shielder.summary: Wedding Carmen protects the highest-ATK ally selected at the first battle’s start. Damage sharing, automatic rescue and party recovery on her basic create a sustained carry-protection kit, while Wedding March provides a targeted cleanse/heal and feeds Chill to Moon allies.
wedding-shielder.watch: ATK ordering can assign the oath to the wrong ally.

wedding-dualsword.dependency_note: She wants enemies that use Barriers and allies that feed Ignition or capitalize on the highest-ATK ally’s turn progress. Without those conditions she loses much of her special utility.

best_partners.why: Harley can grant three Ignition to the highest-ATK Sun ally; set Epindel as that recipient if feeding her is the plan.
Sun turns help upgraded Purewhite Resolve, while Luna supplies defensive support and debuffs to expose the priority target.
Her on-attack CRIT Rate bonus supports Epindel’s allied-critical stack trigger; she can also benefit from Bouquet Toss’s highest-ATK ally gauge reward if geared for it.

wedding-dualsword.summary: Wedding Epindel specializes in attacking Barriers: Bouquet Toss gains extra damage against a shielded target and can advance the highest-ATK teammate if it breaks that Barrier. Sun allies and allied critical hits feed Ignition for her conditional extra turn.
wedding-dualsword.watch: Anti-Barrier payoff shrinks against teams without shields.

bunny-pray.dependency_note: Moon allies attacking grant her turn progress and High Roller chances through Cash In. Pick attackers that benefit from CRIT Rate Up; she still needs a healer or protective teammate.

best_partners.why: Claire's Moon attacks feed Cash In; Frey's CRIT Rate Up helps Where Are You Looking? crit for three Chill.
Professor M is Moon and attacks repeatedly through her own basic and reactive skill; eligible attacks feed Frey while her dual-attack support adds pressure.
Emily is Moon, grants a targeted barrier/ATK Up and attacks while protecting the group; these attacks also feed Cash In.

bunny-pray.summary: Bunny Frey is a Moon damage dealer and CRIT Rate supporter, not the healing Kingdom Frey. She builds High Roller through Bullseye, Chill conversion and Moon allies attacking, then her basic changes into Forced Negotiation at five High Roller on her own turn.
bunny-pray.watch: No healing despite sharing a name with a healer variant.

stranisearl-roseblade.dependency_note: Her ultimate creates its own extra turn and Bloom window. Support improves safety and removes debuffs before her damage check, but no specific teammate is required to enable her basic kit.

best_partners.why: Lumière Sonnet removes two debuffs per ally and advances other allies, helping Amora reach attacks without debuffs.
Protects the highest-ATK ally and provides a targeted full cleanse if Amora receives the oath.
Bind increases all-target damage taken, supporting Light-Forged Execution where the debuff lands.

stranisearl-roseblade.summary: Amora combines an area execution with an explicit extra turn, then uses Nocturnal Bloom to act faster and penetrate DEF. Her passive rewards attacking without debuffs and can convert full Insight into a turn-start cleanse and offensive buffs. Use her when a damage slot must pressure both a wave and its last survivor.
stranisearl-roseblade.watch: Clean-state damage bonus is weakened until debuffs are removed.

halloween-beamsword.dependency_note: Ally turns accelerate Dust Detection, while enemy area attacks advance her next turn. She does not need a specific attribute partner; she needs allies who survive long enough to take turns.

best_partners.why: Emily's targeted Barrier buys time for healing, while her own extra turn provides another ally-turn opportunity for Dust Detection.
Carnelia supplies damage and turn denial; Ceres can heal her after Spoke's once-per-battle lethal-damage survival.
Dana buffs herself and another attacker, while Ceres supplies healing and cleansing that Dana lacks.
Bell's defeat-triggered turn progress helps her keep acting; Ceres protects that damage-and-control slot rather than competing with it.

halloween-beamsword.summary: Ceres in the Sharp & Sweet variant is a team healer whose cleaning counter turns ordinary actions into extra healing. Ally turns build Dust Detection; five stacks let her own action trigger Pre-Arrival Cleanup. Her larger heal also cleanses and supplies team ATK Up, so she contributes to damage without building as an attacker.
halloween-beamsword.watch: The extra Cleanup needs five Dust Detection stacks and one of her own actions.

halloween-rod.dependency_note: Choose an attacking partner with high ATK and area attacks, and arrange for that partner to act before Lydia when possible.

best_partners.why: Carnelia's Dissonance Break hits every enemy and can feed Clocking Out if she receives the highest-ATK mark.
Bell's Condolence hits all enemies and her SPD Up and defeat-triggered turn progress can produce more marked-ally turns.
Emily's targeted Barrier protects Lydia or the marked carry; Turn-Down Service is also an area attack if Emily happens to receive the mark.
Frey provides Barriers and a full single-target cleanse to keep the marked attacker functioning.

halloween-rod.summary: Lydia in the Moon maid variant is a linked damage dealer. She marks the highest-ATK other ally; that ally's turns and attacks build Clocking Out, which turns Lydia's single-target cooldown attacks into stronger area versions. Her strength depends on how reliably the marked ally feeds that five-stack window.
halloween-rod.watch: Highest-ATK targeting can mark the wrong teammate after build changes.

dark-unknown.dependency_note: She supplies her own Shatter, but the team must create and exploit break windows while keeping her alive. Gille directly supports her Shatter state; a defender/healer covers periods without Insight protection.

best_partners.why: Gille's ultimate gives Overture and turn progress to Shatter holders; Dark Asherah supplies that state herself, then creates breaks for Gille's follow-up.
Emily's barrier/ATK Up protects a break carry and boosts ATK-based chain damage without needing Dark Asherah to sacrifice offense.
Dress Asherah heals, cleanses and advances allies, preserving Dark Asherah through repeated boss attacks; they are different slugs with different roles.

dark-unknown.summary: Dark Asherah is a break-focused Order attacker, distinct from her Voyager damage and Dress healing variants. Lucula Noctis supplies Shatter; Phantom Sever then gains substantial Toughness pressure, especially against bosses. Attacking already broken targets resets Phantom Sever and builds Witch's Stigma.
dark-unknown.watch: Much of her damage engine disappears if the target cannot break.

west-lancer.dependency_note: Bring an actual healer and damage dealers. A Star healer such as original Frey can support her, but simply stacking Star allies does not create protection that her base kit lacks.

best_partners.why: Original Frey heals and cleanses allies Besta cannot heal, and her recovery skills have extra benefit for Star targets.
Tanya supplies actual Toughness pressure and team critical support while Besta handles limited defensive duties.
Against area attackers, Roberta's automatic response supplies damage while a Blossom Besta can also respond with Repel.

west-lancer.summary: Besta is a straightforward HP-based defender. Her ordinary kit weakens one enemy's ATK and increases her own DEF, so she is easier to keep alive than her allies. Blossom changes her role substantially by adding ally barriers, team DEF Up and a conditional response to area attacks.
west-lancer.watch: The ordinary kit mostly protects Besta herself.

officer-police.dependency_note: She needs an actual damage dealer and someone who heals or protects the other three allies; her personal recovery cannot cover them.

best_partners.why: Rapid Resupply cleanses and heals a teammate Annah cannot heal.
Annah can reduce the main attacker’s ATK while Luna supplies the area damage missing from her kit.
Lydia slows enemy turns and applies Unknown Hex; Annah supplies personal staying power while Lydia sets up.

officer-police.summary: Annah is a self-sustaining defender who weakens one attacker rather than forcing enemies to hit her. Her base kit heals only herself; Blossom adds team DEF support, a personal shield and conditional counterattacks. Base Annah is useful only if her own survival and one enemy’s ATK Down are what the lineup needs.
officer-police.watch: No taunt or base damage-sharing effect directs attacks away from teammates.

construct-wrench.dependency_note: The ordinary version supplies her own basic buffs but benefits from early crit support and healing. Blossom additionally wants regular cooldown attacks and safe access to broken targets for Hex Nut damage.

best_partners.why: Song of the Toast raises Marcille's ATK; Marcille's Sun turns feed Charlotte's Ignition, giving a reciprocal reason to pair them.
All In supplies CRIT Rate Up to help ordinary Marcille meet her speed/anti-heal crit conditions; Frey is a damage supporter here, not the healer.
Marcille's Burn can feed Serpang's upgraded Burn-enemy-turn passive; he heals Sun allies and lowers enemy Effect RES for debuffs.

construct-wrench.summary: Marcille is a single-target Sun attacker with Burn, a self ATK buff and healing reduction. Her ordinary kit is simple and crit-dependent; her separate Blossom kit adds a much more involved Fractured Nut/Hex Nut cycle. Do not judge the ordinary version as if those Blossom effects are already active.
construct-wrench.watch: Ordinary speed and anti-heal effects depend on crits and last only one turn.

lpu-post.dependency_note: She benefits from a partner who already supplies buffs, but the Express Delivery recipient needs confirmation. Use her for healing if already invested, with protection and offensive support from teammates.

best_partners.why: Emily gives a targeted ATK buff and Barrier plus party DEF Up, covering Vera's lack of direct protection and providing existing buffs.
Dana buffs herself and the highest-ATK other ally and supplies area damage, giving useful buffs independently of Express Delivery.
Carnelia supplies area pressure and Buff Block, while Vera handles recovery after nonlethal damage.
Charlotte supplies deliberate CRIT Rate support and extra-turn offense, so the team need not rely on Vera rolling ATK Up.

lpu-post.summary: Vera is a straightforward HP-scaling healer: one skill heals and removes one debuff from one ally, and her ultimate heals the party. Express Delivery adds random utility, but its recipient is inconsistent between the ultimate description and effect record, so it should not be the reason a team depends on her.
lpu-post.watch: Random buffs cannot replace a deliberate offensive or defensive tool.

noa-observer.dependency_note: She can apply SPD Down herself, but partners with reliable useful debuffs reduce setup dependence. A protector and healer cover her missing survival tools; an all-Star team is unnecessary unless it serves another kit.

best_partners.why: Bell supplies Silence or ACC Down for Naru's conditional special while removing buffs and handling area damage.
Naru's Star attacks feed Dana's unlocked Leap passive; Dana can buff Naru if she is the highest-ATK other ally.
Emily provides ATK Up and a Barrier to protect Naru's damage turns.
Ceres heals, cleanses and buffs ATK so Naru can spend actions attacking rather than recovering.

noa-observer.summary: Naru is a single-target attacker with a simple debuff setup: Beyond Expectations! attempts SPD Down, then Behold My Skill! deals more damage to a debuffed enemy. The bonus accepts any debuff, so an ally can establish the condition without waiting for Naru's ultimate.
noa-observer.watch: Only single-target damage and no party utility in the ordinary kit.

maid-spear.dependency_note: Her attacks work on their own, but an external lasting buff makes Final Service's extra progress easier to use. She needs healing and protection rather than an attribute-matched teammate for its own sake.

best_partners.why: Emily gives Claire a three-turn ATK buff and Barrier, providing both a useful buff condition and protection.
Ceres supplies team ATK Up, healing and cleansing, helping Claire stay active.
Charlotte's CRIT Rate buff and possible ATK Up can qualify Claire's buff condition while improving damage.
Bell supplies buff removal, Silence and area damage, covering jobs Claire cannot perform.

maid-spear.summary: Claire is a single-target attacker who gives herself brief SPD Up and gains progress toward her next turn from Final Service. That ultimate gains more progress if she already has a buff, so a real ally buff is useful rather than treating every attack as an identical rotation.
maid-spear.watch: No area attack or enemy debuff.

maid-scissors.dependency_note: She can apply her own Burn, but its cooldown and the brief extra Burn make an allied Burn source useful. Cristelle specifically turns Scarlet's Sun attacking skills and Burn into a larger linked team plan.

best_partners.why: Cristelle can apply broad Burn, extend a target's Burn and gain Ignition from Scarlet's attacking Sun cooldown skills.
Charlotte can supply CRIT Rate and an upgrade-dependent ATK buff, and adds ATK Down for defense.
Ceres supplies healing, cleansing and party ATK support that Scarlet lacks.
Emily protects Scarlet with a targeted Barrier and buffs her ATK without needing Scarlet to debuff first.

maid-scissors.summary: Scarlet is a single-target Burn attacker. Her ultimate applies Burn and may add another instance, then Let's Heat Things Up! deals more damage against a burning enemy. Her passive only increases HP, so most of her offensive value comes from active skills and ATK investment.
maid-scissors.watch: No area damage, healing or ally protection.

magician-sniper.dependency_note: Her own speed buff and attacks function without a specific teammate. Partners should provide healing, protection and stronger buffs or debuffs; the ag-manip tag refers to her conditional Nova option.

best_partners.why: Dana can buff Clarissa if she is the highest-ATK other ally; Clarissa's Star attacks feed Dana's unlocked passive.
Emily's targeted ATK buff and Barrier protect an attacker who has no self-heal.
Frey provides Barriers, cleansing and enhanced healing to Star Clarissa.
Bell supplies buff removal and Silence that Clarissa lacks, and can contribute area damage.

magician-sniper.summary: Clarissa is a simple single-target attacker with enemy SPD Down and personal SPD Up. Her passive only adds CRIT Rate. She can contribute a clear job with an existing build, but offers little team protection or offensive support beyond slowing one target.
magician-sniper.watch: No area damage or ally buff.

counterside-hilde.dependency_note: Use Hilde to buy time for a damage or support engine.

best_partners.why: Hilde's Sun turns feed Charlotte's Ignition, while her opening barriers cover Song of the Toast setup.
Opening protection gives Tyria time to mark enemies; keeping Tyria alive also keeps her Thorns active.
Serpang heals the party, gives stronger recovery to Sun allies and can weaken the taunted enemy's ATK.

counterside-hilde.summary: Hilde is a Sun defender whose HP supports both damage and barriers. Her opening passive shields the other allies, Buster Overdrive gives her a durable personal defensive state, and Dragon Buster helps her resist debuffs and take hits. Her taunt is selective rather than teamwide.
counterside-hilde.watch: No party heal or cleanse for prolonged damage.

counterside-mina.dependency_note: She generates her own Leap and self buffs. External protection, timely ATK support and an enemy resistance reducer are useful; she has no mandatory faction partner.

best_partners.why: Lyn's Clear Wind branch can grant three Leap to Star allies, helping Mina reach the special's extra-Bleed condition, and adds Star-team CRIT DMG support.
Emily supplies a barrier and ATK Up for Mina's ATK-based attacks and Bleed while keeping her alive through ramp.
Serpang's Effect RES Down supports Bleed attempts and his party healing covers Mina's lack of recovery; it is not an immunity bypass.

counterside-mina.summary: Yoo Mina combines area Bleed application with a crit-driven personal turn cycle. She builds ATK after attacks, speeds toward her next turn when she crits, and can add area chain damage through Catalyst if that potential is available. She is a damage dealer rather than a control character.
counterside-mina.watch: Bleed is poor into Immunity or frequent cleansing.

counterside-rosaria.dependency_note: Rosaria supplies her own Inferno route, Agitation and area DEF Down. External early crit support and recovery improve consistency; another Chaos unit is not required merely to make her kit function.

best_partners.why: All In gives party CRIT Rate Up before Rosaria's area attack, improving the chance of building Inferno from multiple targets.
Emily protects Rosaria with a targeted barrier and ATK Up, especially valuable after the one-time survival trigger is spent.
Party healing and cleanse restore Rosaria after her low-HP safeguard, while allied turn progress helps continue the damage window.

counterside-rosaria.summary: Rosaria is a fast Chaos area attacker who turns critical hits into Inferno stacks for a focused follow-up window. Difference in Class combines a large hit, DEF Down and 50% progress toward her next turn; Ruler's Judgement spends Inferno, adding an automatic basic at three stacks.
counterside-rosaria.watch: Survival protection is once per battle and does not replace healing.
